clue.text: Skilful, confining English to a rout

indicators.note: confining means holding something within, so the skilful word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: deft means skilful or nimble

explanation.surface: A clever team keeps an Englishman in check and ends up winning by a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confining' puts E and A inside DEFT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing loss, a heavy beating in battle or sport.

clue.text: It's rased in storm or other catastrophe

indicators.note: letters caught in a storm are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something razed to the ground in a gale is one more calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in storm' rearranges the letters of IT'S RASED; 'or other' links the wordplay to the definition, as the storm is itself a calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a sudden calamity bringing great damage or loss.

clue.text: Source of warmth is thick coat, new one

parts.note: an animal's thick coat is its fur
an ace is a one on dice or cards

explanation.surface: A heavy coat, bought new, keeps one warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace is an enclosed fire chamber that produces intense heat.

clue.text: Aircraft instrument to change covering a period

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the word for change goes around the period

parts.note: to alter is to change
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: Pilots must adjust a gauge over a stretch of the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts TIME inside ALTER; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is the cockpit dial that shows a plane's height.

clue.text: Ancient civilization isn't represented at back of incomplete maps

indicators.note: at back of places the rearranged letters after the shortened word
incomplete means the book of maps loses its last letter

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: represented in the sense of shown in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lost ancient culture is absent from the back pages of a partial map book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts ATLAS to ATLA; 'represented' rearranges ISN'T to NTIS, which goes 'at back of' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island realm said by Plato to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Vermin controlled by docker?

parts.note: a docker here is one who docks tails; in the nursery rhyme a farmer's wife cuts off the tails of three sightless rodents with a carving knife

explanation.surface: Rats on the quayside are kept down by a dock worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docker' suggests a port worker, but it means one who docks, or cuts short, tails, as the farmer's wife does in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme mice have their tails cut off with a carving knife by the farmer's wife.

clue.text: A second complete collection is a valuable item

parts.note: a set is a complete collection of things

explanation.surface: A full matched collection is a prized possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something of worth that someone owns.

clue.text: Part of rigging, raised a little, to feel wrong

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a spot is a little, as in a spot of tea
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: Part of a ship's rigging, hoisted a bit, seems out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SPOT upwards into TOPS, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest sail on a mast, part of a ship's rig.

clue.text: Slim second volume's the best, if one's skipping

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for volume

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so the numeral for one drops from the word for the best

parts.note: the elite are the best of a group
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The slimmer second book is the finest, if a chapter is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping' drops I from ELITE to leave ELTE; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte describes a slender, graceful figure.

clue.text: Vehicles set alight in film

definitions.meaning: read literally, horse-drawn war carts that are burning
the 1981 British film about runners at the 1924 Olympics

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, burning war carts; also the title of the Oscar-winning 1981 film about British Olympic athletes.

clue.text: It extends support for medical emergencies

definitions.meaning: something that stretches or lengthens a thing
a frame for carrying the sick or injured

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a thing that pulls something longer; also the litter used to carry a casualty.

clue.text: Composer cutting short meal

indicators.note: cutting short means removing the end, so the meal loses its last letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A musician trims back his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of light operettas.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppé wrote operettas and overtures such as Light Cavalry.

clue.text: Problem leading to start of speech being repeated

definitions.text: Problem leading to start of speech being repeated

parts.words: Problem leading to start of speech being repeated
parts.note: describes a speech impediment in which the opening sound of a word is said over and over

explanation.surface: A trouble causes the opening of an address to be given twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a speech given again from the top; it describes a speaker repeating first sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment where the opening sounds of words are repeated involuntarily.

clue.text: Competitor, in the event, ran third

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A runner in the race came in third place.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'evENT RAN Third'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a contest.

clue.text: Calm, then tense? It happens

indicators.note: then places the second piece after the first

parts.note: even means calm or steady, as in an even temper
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Steady, then nervous: a question of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that takes place.

clue.text: Line in translation of Fidelio? It's rigged

indicators.note: in places the line's letter inside the rearranged opera name
a translation renders something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lyric in a new version of Beethoven's opera seems to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera; its letters, rearranged, take in L. 'It's rigged' is not cheating but drilling rigs.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil field is an area dotted with drilling rigs extracting petroleum.

clue.text: Fashionable military leader is not particular

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a general is a senior army commander

explanation.surface: A trendy army commander is easygoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means broadly or as a rule, as opposed to specifically.

clue.text: Article's attempt to capture church's history

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside, so the church letters sit within the other pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a try is an attempt
CE is Church of England, followed by the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece seeks to record a parish's past.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is one's line of descent, a family's history.

clue.text: Jail is prepared after one politician's end in dishonour

indicators.note: after places the last two pieces behind the first three

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: end in picks the final letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
on means ready or willing, as in 'I'm on'

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician is ready for a cell after his downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end in' gives R, the last letter of 'dishonour'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to lock them up, as a verb.

clue.text: Family of writers with German, supporting Germany

parts.note: mit is German for with
for means in support of
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Literary relatives associated with a German, backing their country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mitford sisters, among them Nancy and Jessica, were a famous English literary family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mitfords were an aristocratic English family including novelist Nancy and writer Jessica.

clue.text: Board to show greater antiquity

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to climb aboard it
to grow older, as in 'getting on a bit'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to climb aboard a vehicle and to advance in years.

clue.text: One steals leftover bit of drink

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang this rhymes with thief
a fragment left in the bottom of a cuppa

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang uses the leftover from a cup of tea for 'thief'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a thief; also a fragment left in the bottom of a cuppa.

clue.text: A bomb going up, trapping Government, is a mystery

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the reversed letters enclose the government letter
going up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mine is an explosive bomb

explanation.surface: Why a bomb exploding inside Whitehall is a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses A MINE to ENIMA; 'trapping' puts G inside; 'is a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or riddle, something baffling.

clue.text: A pint? Absolutely!

definitions.meaning: a full pint is twice a half-pint measure in a British pub
British slang meaning very much so, a strong yes

explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub beer is sold by the pint or the half pint; the phrase is also an emphatic British 'yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A full pint is literally more than a half measure; the phrase is also British slang for an emphatic yes.

clue.text: Minister offering no opening for crime

indicators.note: offering no opening means the first letter is left off

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman without an introduction commits an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Collection of pictures depicting time on French peak

indicators.note: on in an across clue places one piece after the other

parts.note: mont is French for mountain
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An album portraying the long years spent on an Alpine summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depicting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A montage is a composite image made by putting several pictures together.

clue.text: Good area of Scotland? That's outrageous

parts.note: Ross is a region of the Scottish Highlands, as in Ross and Cromarty

explanation.surface: A fine Highland district? Shocking!
explanation.walkthrough: Ross is a historic district of the Scottish Highlands. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means flagrant or shocking, as in gross misconduct.

clue.text: Briefly including Rector's wrong, wrong

parts.note: inc. is a short form of including

indicators.note: wrong signals that the clergyman's letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A rector shown to be mistaken, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'wrong' rearranges RECTOR to ORRECT; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect means not right or mistaken.

clue.text: French area Andersen represented

indicators.note: represented in the sense of presented anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A region of France is depicted by the Danish fairy-tale writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes is a forested region spanning north-east France, Belgium and Luxembourg.

clue.text: Very furry hare taking in expert? Not at first

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the word for hare surrounds the trimmed expert

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, to fly

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: A downy hare welcomes a specialist, though not to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hare' is a verb, to rush, so FLY; 'Not at first' cuts BUFF to UFF, which FLY is 'taking in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluffy describes something covered in soft fur or down.
